columns.label: Ebook
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily get and consume ebooks on the platform (free or paid) as a first-class product, open, buy, borrow, or read without hunting.

columns.label: Short-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily consume short-form video as a first-class surface (For You, Reels, Shorts).

columns.label: Long-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch creator / UGC long-form video (or specialty long video) as a core surface. Course lectures belong under Courses. Hollywood catalogs belong under Series/Films.

columns.label: Series/Films
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch series and films as an SVOD / catalog entertainment product.

columns.label: Courses
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily take or browse structured courses as a first-class product.

columns.label: Newsletters
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily read or subscribe to newsletters / creator writing as a first-class product.

columns.label: Audio
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily listen to music, podcasts, or audiobooks as a first-class product.

columns.label: Memberships
columns.definition: Yes if a creator or seller can accept payments from others and make money through the platform, checkout, fan subscriptions, tips, ads, shop, or creator funds. Not only a classic Patreon-style membership product.

columns.label: Community & Messaging
columns.definition: Yes if you can create or join a group, community, or club, including group chats, Groups, subreddits, community tabs, discussion boards, or community feeds. A one-off comment on a single video or listing is not the bar; a durable place for the group to talk is.

columns.label: Storefronts
columns.definition: Yes if the product gives a creator a custom storefront or site that can take the place of building their own website (bio page, creator site, branded shop). Not a shop tab on someone else’s multi-seller marketplace.

columns.label: Marketplaces
columns.definition: Yes if a typical person can search and shop a catalog of offerings from many sellers, courses, books, digital goods, etc. Storefront software (Shopify, WooCommerce) is not a marketplace unless shoppers browse many sellers there.

scaleFacts: Positioned as a direct-to-fan sales platform/marketplace for creators, authors sell directly while keeping 100% of list price and IP ownership.
Creator Studio: free signup, upload ebooks/audiobooks/music/video, set pricing, bundle formats, publish shareable links; storefront pages, checkout, giveaways, and anonymized analytics on paid plans.
Creators get 100% of purchase price; Curios monetizes via ~8% buyer-side payment/platform fee and author plan thresholds (free plan: USD 0.50/sale after the 10th sale in a month unless upgraded).
iOS/Android apps for reading, listening, and watching purchased content from favorite authors/creators.

strengths.title: Full revenue to creators, minimal middlemen
strengths.detail: Creators receive 100% of list price, positioned as simpler than multi-middleman retailer/aggregator stacks.

strengths.title: Direct customer relationships and data
strengths.detail: Authors get buyer emails and engagement analytics (downloads, listening progress) on paid plans, strong for community and repeat sales.

strengths.title: Bundling and flexible storefronts
strengths.detail: Bundle ebook + audiobook, custom storefront pages, and direct checkout links that feel seamless from an author’s site.

strengths.title: Curated consumer app for discovery and consumption
strengths.detail: Reader apps offer a streaming-like experience for books and audio, supports recurring engagement beyond one-off purchases.

weaknesses.title: Smaller audience vs major retailers
weaknesses.detail: Discovery and scale lag Amazon, Audible, or Kobo, creators must drive their own traffic.

weaknesses.title: Platform fees and plan thresholds can be confusing
weaknesses.detail: Mix of buyer-side fees (~8%) and author-side thresholds is more complex than simple royalty-rate models.

weaknesses.title: Ecosystem still emerging
weaknesses.detail: Fewer third-party tools, tutorials, and integrations than legacy self-publishing platforms.

content:
Kahana is a library of curated hubs, Explore, Clubs, and optional Stripe. Curios is direct-to-fan author storefronts, ebook/audio delivery, and reader apps. They overlap in places and diverge in others.

What each one is

Kahana is built around hubs people can open, Explore so strangers can find them, Aura as scarce daily recognition, and Clubs so discussion outlives a feed. Selling stays optional.

Curios is a direct-to-fan sales and streaming platform that lets authors, artists, and creators build storefronts, sell ebooks and audio, and deliver content to readers via the Curios apps while keeping 100% of list price. Official site.

Why this comparison

This article puts Kahana and Curios side by side. It covers what each supports as a first-class product job, key features, and a few research notes so you have a clearer picture of what they are, how they compare, and what you can actually do on each one. It is not a teardown, and it is not a switch-tomorrow pitch.

One naming note: Kahana was previously called Curio. This article compares Kahana to Curios (curios.com / studio.curios.com), a separate direct-to-fan author platform. They are not the same product.
contentAfter:
What you can do on each

On Kahana you can publish a hub, list it on Explore, discuss it in a Club, grant Aura, and turn on a Stripe paywall when you are ready to charge.

On Curios you can use Ebook, Audio, Memberships, Storefronts, and Marketplaces as first-class product jobs. You only need niche author tooling: studio uploads, 100% of list price, bundles, and a consumer app for purchased books and audio.

Using Kahana with Curios

You can use both. Curios keeps doing what it already does well. Kahana is another place to package the work, get discovered, and grow an audience.

Keep Curios for author storefronts and in-app reading if that tooling is useful. Run clubs, discussion, and library discovery on Kahana so the book is a shared shelf, not only a checkout and a reader.
